_notes: 30 frames at 200 ms, voice 0.5 everywhere. A (x 400) alternates mouth 0.1/0.3 on frames 0-14 (0.3 on odd frames 1-13), then 0.1. B (x 1300) is 0.1 until frame 14, then 0.3 on odd frames from 15.

Lips = min(1, std of mouth within 500 ms / 0.05): a window of up to 5 frames holding both 0.1 and 0.3 gives std >= 0.08, so 1; a flat window gives 0. A: 1 on frames 0-15 (frame 15's window reaches frame 13), 0 from 16. B: 0 on frames 0-12, 1 from 13 (frame 13's window reaches frame 15).
No pan, so score = (0.6 lips + 0.05 continuity) / 0.65.
Frame 0: nobody is current, A is the only candidate, A becomes current. Frames 13-15: A 1.0, B 0.923, both above 0.5 with moving lips: an overlap of 600 ms (< 1.5 s), so it stays A.

Frame 16: A 0.077 (lips 0, not a candidate), B 0.923 > 0.077 + 0.15, so B claims from frame 16 (3.2 s) and keeps the claim. Balanced hold = 1 s: at frame 21 (4.2 s) B takes over, back-dated to frame 16.
Segments: A [0, 3.2 s), B [3.2 s, 6 s), both longer than the 1 s minimum.

Window for 1920x1080 to 9:16: h = min(1080, floor(1920*1920/1080)) = 1080, w = round(1080*1080/1920) = round(607.5) = 608, so a centre x lies in [304, 1616] and y is always 540 (the window is as tall as the frame).
A face at x = 400 (w 200) has its centre at 500; at x = 1300, at 1400.
Faces never move, so each segment has one cut key. Upscale 1920 / 1080 = 1.78 <= 2: not low quality.
